problem: Visual navigation policies are usually trained from scratch with RL for each task (ObjectNav, RoomNav, AudioNav, ImageNav) and each goal modality. This needs tens to hundreds of millions of interactions per task, task-specific priors or annotations, and prior transfer methods only pretrain the observation encoder, so a new policy is still learned from scratch. Existing ImageNav SOTA also relies on panoramic 360° sensors.
motivation: Different semantic navigation tasks share a common skill: searching a 3D scene for something described semantically. If you know how to find a microwave, finding a kitchen, or finding an object from a sketch or its sound, should be easy. Image-goals can be sampled freely without annotations and carry rich appearance and context cues, so a policy trained to find random views should learn general semantic search priors. These priors could then be reused for new goal types with no new interaction, which the paper calls zero-shot experience learning (ZSEL).
key_idea: Train one semantic search policy on annotation-free image-goal navigation using a view-alignment reward and goal-view augmentation. Then train small goal encoders for other modalities (label, sketch, audio, edgemap) offline to map into the frozen image-goal embedding space. Plugging a new encoder into the unchanged policy solves new tasks zero-shot, or after brief fine-tuning.
insight: Rewarding the agent for reducing its angle to the goal view once within 1 m forces it to ground the image-goal semantics rather than just the distance signal. Ablation on Gibson split A: View Reward Only 24.4/17.3 SR/SPL and View Aug. Only 22.0/18.8, versus full 29.2/21.6 and DTG-RL 22.6/18.0, so the two components are complementary. The modular-transfer ablation (Fig. 4 left, ObjectNav-Label) shows transferring only the goal encoder or only the policy gives no gain over no-transfer, and only the observation encoder helps. The full plug-and-play transfer is what gives large gains and enables ZSEL. A PointNav-pretrained policy (DD-PPO) transfers 5–14 SR points worse than the ImageNav semantic search policy, so the source task matters. ZSEL performance grows with source-task (ImageNav) experience. Raising RGB resolution from 128 to 256 boosts ZSEL more than adding depth+pose.
method: Semantic search policy for ImageNav: ResNet9 observation encoder f_O, ResNet9 image-goal encoder f_G^I, and a 2-layer GRU (128-d) actor-critic policy, trained end-to-end with PPO/DD-PPO on RGB-only 90° FoV observations.

View reward: r_t = reduced geodesic distance + [d_t ≤ 1 m]·reduced angle to the goal view − 0.01 slack. Success reward R_s = 5×([d≤d_s] + [d≤d_s and α≤25°]), so the agent is pushed to look at the goal view when near it.

View augmentation: each training episode keeps start p0 and goal location pG fixed but samples the goal image I_G from a random heading at pG. This regularizes the policy and teaches spatial co-occurrence priors (e.g., chairs seen near a dining table).

Joint goal embedding: new modality encoders f_G^M are trained offline, with f_G^I frozen, using a cosine loss (1−cos for matched image–goal pairs, max(0,cos) for mismatched pairs). Encoders are ResNet9 for sketch, edgemap and audio spectrograms, and a 2-layer MLP for labels. Pairs come from small offline datasets (14K object images, 20K room images, 170K edgemap views) whose annotations are automatic detections from 3D Scene Graph models.

Plug & play transfer / ZSEL: f_G^I is replaced by f_G^M and the policy acts as a_t ~ π(f_O(o_t), f_G^M(g)) with no target-task interaction. Optionally the whole model (f_O, f_G, π) is fine-tuned with RL on the target task, for up to 20M steps.

setting.backbone: ResNet9 observation/goal encoders + 2-layer GRU (128) actor-critic, trained from scratch with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: Source: Gibson ImageNav (Mezghani et al. dataset), 72 training scenes × 9K episodes, 50K updates = 500M frames. Offline goal-embedding data: 14K object images, 20K room images, 170K edgemap views from training scenes, auto-labeled with 3D Scene Graph model predictions; sketches from Eitz et al. (70/category train); audio clips from the SAVi dataset (6 train clips). Optional fine-tuning: up to 20M RL steps per target task on 24 Gibson-tiny scenes.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB only, 128×128, 90° FoV (no depth, no GPS/compass); goal given as image / label / sketch / 4 s audio clip / edgemap
setting.action_space: low-level MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT / TURN_RIGHT 30° / STOP
setting.privileged: none at test time (the view reward uses GT distance/angle to goal only during training)

Several results appear only as curves: training curves for transfer (Fig. 3/7), the modular-transfer ablation and source-experience scalability (Fig. 4), long-term Task Expert training to 500M steps (Fig. 5/8), and the sensor ablation RGB vs RGB+Depth+Pose vs RGB-256 (Fig. 9). The main text refers to the Gibson ImageNav table as 'Table 4', but the main table is Table 1 and Table 4 is the per-difficulty breakdown. Ablation rows 'View Aug. Only' (22.0/18.8) and 'View Reward Only' (24.4/17.3) on split A are omitted from numbers. The ImageNav and downstream episode sets are non-standard, author-sampled, RGB-only setups; for Gibson ImageNav the 14 unseen scenes are the standard Gibson val scenes, which the paper calls 'test'.
results: On RGB-only 90°-FoV Gibson ImageNav the policy reaches 29.2 SR / 21.6 SPL on split A, +6.6 SR over the DTG-reward RL baseline (22.6/18.0). Mezghani et al. drops to 9.0 SR without a panorama. On split B it reaches 33.0/23.6 versus Hahn et al. 24.0/12.4, which uses RGB-D, pose and a 120° FoV. It also leads cross-domain on MP3D (14.6/10.8) and HM3D (9.6/6.3). When transferred and fine-tuned for 20M steps, it beats all transfer baselines on all five downstream tasks, e.g. ObjectNav-Label 21.9 vs 15.6 (Zhou et al.) and RoomNav 27.9 vs 13.9 (DD-PPO PointNav transfer). Its ZSEL variant beats the from-scratch Task Expert on 4 of 5 tasks with zero target experience; the Task Expert needs about 507M total steps to match ZSEL.
limitations: Absolute success rates remain low (RGB-only, 128×128). ZSEL is weak for audio goals (4.4 vs Task Expert 6.6), and ViewNav-Edgemap stays below 8% SR.
Handles only single-goal semantic navigation. Multi-goal or instruction-following tasks like VLN are not addressed, and positive transfer is not guaranteed for target tasks dissimilar from ImageNav.

Downstream evaluation uses small custom Gibson-tiny splits (5 test scenes, own episodes) rather than standard ObjectNav benchmarks. Common failure modes: early stopping and misestimating the goal viewpoint.
